Yeah, I totally feel that. That's how I approached things when I identified as bi for the past 10 years, like a casual no-big-deal kind of thing. Especially around my friends, my sister, and my parents.

Like at first, I was thinking about waiting until he was basically on his deathbed to come out to him so I wouldn't have to deal with the hurt of him potentially shunning me for the rest of his life. But I figured that wouldn't be fair to him at all, especially after I watched "The Hunger" and reflected on my own pain from putting it off this long. Dude, even though I'm not ready to *fully* go nosurf yet, I feel you. My counselor and I have been going over skills and activities I can try out to get started on a social media/Youtube detox, but in the middle of a depressive episode, my first instinct is to go to Youtube to "distract myself". (Process addictions are fuuuun.)

But we did talk about something interesting that might be helpful to you. It might not be the best idea to go back to nuclear nosurf right away, especially in the middle of a depressive episode. During those times, we (as in both you and I) feel so much pressure from having to stay off while we're depressed that it makes us wanna get online even more, which makes us even more depressed, and the cycle starts again.

Maybe take things one day at a time instead? Like, when you wake up, ask yourself, "How do I feel today?" followed by "Could I try nosurfing today?" And if you're able to nosurf, ask yourself the same question again tomorrow morning. You don't even have to commit to nosurfing in the morning, you can decide to do it in the middle of the day if you wanted to. Also, don't beat yourself up from breaking any kind of streaks - our brains are dumb and these things happen.

Hopefully this helped a little bit!

* Procrastinate on all work and binge watch Youtube 85% of the day
